target: PleasantOther consensus (annotation col 3), HRF-convolved, placed at film onset
mask: posterior MNI gray matter, y < -60 mm, 43683 voxels
significance: withheld project-wide; descriptive effect sizes only
qc_note: five lowest-motion Payload runs, pre-registered by mriqc fd_mean BEFORE any decode; sub-S07 (the June-7 PoC subject) ranked 28/30 at fd_mean 0.346 and is excluded

positive_control_pooled.description: signal planted at each timescale, recovered via leave-one-subject-out; a valid estimator must recover the ~100s valence timescale
positive_control_pooled.verdict: PASS - strong and uniform across timescales; the estimator can detect signal at the valence timescale

real_valence_pooled.description: real human PleasantOther valence, leave-one-subject-out, scored within each held-out subject
real_valence_pooled.verdict: NULL - the real decode sits below/inside its own circular-shift null

runs.subject: sub-S07
runs.note: highest-motion run in the dataset; the retracted June-7 PoC

runs.subject: sub-S31
runs.note: lowest-motion ToS run; opposite sign to S07 on the SAME film

single_subject_summary.verdict: single-subject estimation FAILS the positive control at the valence timescale (recovers only +0.147 with a planted signal at SNR 2.0); single-subject estimates are unstable and non-replicating

conclusion: Controlled null. Occipital decoding of PleasantOther valence is not estimable above chance on Emo-FilM, single-subject or pooled across five subjects. The positive control passes on the pooled estimator while the real decode is at chance (+0.033 vs null +0.044 +/- 0.013). This is the same ~80-110s autocorrelation-vs-duration wall the label and inference arms reach, from the neural side.
